title: Log regularity is preserved by generization
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a locally Noetherian fine saturated log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $x,y\in |X|$ with $y$ a generization of $x$, meaning $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$. Suppose $(X,M)$ is log regular at $x$: for a geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], with strict local ring $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, characteristic monoid $P=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ and ideal $I$ generated by the structural images of nonunit log sections, $A/I$ is regular and
$$\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}P^{\rm gp}.$$
Then $(X,M)$ is log regular at $y$ in the same sense. In particular, an fs log structure on the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring is log regular at every point if it is log regular at the closed point. No openness of the regular locus, excellence, or regularity of the underlying scheme is assumed.

source.place: VI 1.2--1.3, printed p.69: log regularity at a point and preservation at every generization, referring to Kato 1994, 7.1. In ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve this serves proof Step 3, regular local model and purity; here it promotes the invariant strict-local ring condition in VI 3.7(c) to log regularity on its local spectrum.

proof.text: Fix the geometric point $\bar x$ in the hypothesis and put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$. Apply [lem-per-pointwise-log-regular-completion], which assumes log regularity only at this point, to choose the sharp characteristic monoid $P$, its pointed etale chart, and the monomial-compatible presentation of $C=\widehat A$ as $B_k(P,n)$, $k$ the residue field of $A$, if $A$ contains a field, or otherwise as $B_V(P,n)/(\theta)$, where $V$ is a Cohen ring for $k$ (the Cohen ring called $C$ in that node) and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_V(P,n)$. For a monoid element $q\in P$ write $a(q)\in A$ for the image of $\alpha(a(q))$ under the chart $a$ (later steps use the same notation $a(\cdot)$); the presentation sends $a(q)$ to $z^q$. Both $A$ and $C$ are nonzero Noetherian local rings. Give $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the pullback log structure from $X$; the chosen $P$-chart is a chart of precisely this structure.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70; pointwise hypothesis as in VI 1.2.

proof.text: Choose a geometric point $\bar y$ above the given generization $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-specialization-strict-local-lift] it lifts to a geometric point $\bar v$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ over $\bar y$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be its underlying prime, $D=A_{\mathfrak q}$ and $L=D^{\rm sh}$ for this geometric point. The structural map $\rho:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is locally ind-etale: restrict $X$ to an affine neighbourhood of $x$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-small-strict-henselization-ind-etale]. Consequently [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies the canonical strict localization $(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar v)}=\operatorname{Spec}L$ with $X_{(\bar y)}$ over $X$. Because the log structure on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is pulled back from $X$, the two pulled-back log structures agree under this isomorphism. It remains to verify the stratum condition and dimension equality on $L$.

source.place: VI 1.3, printed p.69, strict-local reduction; Tag 0GJ5 (remark-can-lift), Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), Tag 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite).

proof.text:
The canonical map $A	o C$ is faithfully flat and surjective on spectra by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Choose a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ contracting to $\mathfrak q$ and put $E=C_{\mathfrak Q}$. The induced map $D	o E$ is a flat local map of Noetherian local rings by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps]. Let $F=\{p\in P:a(p)
otin\mathfrak q\}$. Since the presentations preserve monomials and $\mathfrak Q\cap A=\mathfrak q$, this is exactly $\{p:z^p
otin\mathfrak Q\}$. Define $T=P_F/F^{m gp}$, $I_D=(a(p):p
otin F)D$, and $J=I_DE$. Apply [lem-per-complete-toric-face-strata] to this prime of this presentation: $E/J$ is regular local and $\dim E=\dim(E/J)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{m gp}$.

The quotient map $D/I_D\to E/J$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-quotient-flat] applied to the flat $D$-module $E$. It is local because $D\to E$ is local and $I_D\subset\mathfrak m_D$. Both quotients are Noetherian local rings (their ideals correspond to ideals containing the quotient ideal in the Noetherian source). Since $E/J$ is regular, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] gives that $D/I_D$ is regular. Put $H=E/\mathfrak m_DE$ and $h=\dim H$. The closed fibre of $D/I_D\to E/J$ is also $H$, since $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_DE$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the two flat local maps to get
$$\dim E=\dim D+h,\qquad \dim(E/J)=\dim(D/I_D)+h.$$
Inserting these into step 3 and cancelling $h$ gives
$$\dim D=\dim(D/I_D)+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}T^{\rm gp}.$$
All these dimensions are finite, since they are dimensions of Noetherian local rings. The argument uses no regularity of the formal fibre $H$.

Pass from $D$ to $L=D^{\rm sh}$. This ring is Noetherian by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. By [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient-core], $L/I_DL$ is the strict henselization of $D/I_D$ for the compatible residue-field closure. Hence it is regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. Applying [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] separately to $D$ and $D/I_D$ gives
$$\dim L=\dim D,\qquad\dim(L/I_DL)=\dim(D/I_D).$$
For the chart on $\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] identifies the characteristic at $\bar v$ with $T=P_F/F^{\rm gp}$. Its associated-log-stalk pushout in [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification] shows that its nonunit ideal is $I_DL$: every log section is a chart section times a unit, the chart sections in $F$ become units, and the others generate exactly this ideal. Thus step 4 yields the required regular stratum quotient and dimension equality for this geometric log stalk. The isomorphism over $X$ of step 2 identifies this with the condition at $\bar y$. Since $\bar y$ was arbitrary, $X$ is log regular at $y$.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.3, printed p.69, and VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98; Tags 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular), 06LK (lemma-henselization-dimension).

proof.text: For $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian local and closed point $\mathfrak m$, every prime $\mathfrak p$ satisfies $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus $\mathfrak m\in V(\mathfrak p)=\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}$, so every point is a generization of the closed point. Apply the conclusion already proved to each $\mathfrak p$. By the definition of log regularity in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], the fs log scheme is therefore log regular everywhere.
